backlog.title: Self-update core — stagecoach upgrade (FR-U1–U12, → G26)
backlog.description: Implement the install-method-aware, delegate-first self-updater: detect how the binary was installed and delegate to that channel's native updater wherever one exists, falling back to a SHA256-verified, atomic, rollback-able direct-binary swap ONLY for the direct-binary channel. Walled off from the commit-generation core (no repo/lock/index/provider interaction). Supersedes the v2.1 self-update rejection. See plan/017_397abce9deb1/architecture/{system_context,external_deps,v3_scope_boundary}.md.

milestones.title: Foundation: comparable version, exit code 6, [upgrade] config table, GitHub Releases client
milestones.description: The reusable primitives every upgrade path consumes: a comparable (semver) version of the running binary, the UpdateAvailable=6 exit code, the global-only [upgrade] config table (channel/source_repo), and the HTTP client for the GitHub Releases API (the one named network exception to §19). All injectable/mockable for tests.

tasks.title: Comparable version + exit code 6
tasks.description: Add the UpdateAvailable=6 exit code and a comparable version representation of the running binary (distinct from main.go's display-only resolveVersion).

subtasks.title: Add UpdateAvailable=6 exit code + For()/sentinel wiring
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/017_397abce9deb1/architecture/system_context.md §'Conventions'. internal/exitcode/exitcode.go defines the const block (Success=0, Error=1, NothingToCommit=2, Rescue=3, Busy=5, Timeout=124) and For(err) which maps errors→codes via ExitError + sentinel errors.Is branches. §15.4 adds code 6 = UpdateAvailable (FR-U6, FR-U12). v3_scope_boundary.md: 6 is upgrade-path ONLY, never returned by the commit path.
2. INPUT: internal/exitcode/exitcode.go (the const block + For() + ExitError + New). No new dependencies.
3. LOGIC: (a) Add `UpdateAvailable = 6` to the const block with a comment citing PRD §15.4/FR-U12. (b) Add a sentinel error `ErrUpdateAvailable` (mirrors generate.ErrNothingToCommit style) OR document that callers use `exitcode.New(exitcode.UpdateAvailable, nil)`. PRD FR-U12 says exit 6 = '--check found a newer version (informational)'. Implement For() so that `errors.Is(err, ErrUpdateAvailable)` → UpdateAvailable AND keep the existing `errors.As(err, &ee)` path so `New(UpdateAvailable, nil)` also maps to 6. (c) Do NOT touch any commit-path mapping; 6 must be unreachable from commit-path errors (assert in test).
4. OUTPUT: Modified exitcode.go. New tests in exitcode_test.go following the existing table-driven TestFor pattern (add rows: ErrUpdateAvailable→6; New(6,nil)→6; and a test that commit-path sentinels still map to their codes — regression guard). go test ./internal/exitcode/ passes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] update the file's package doc comment to mention code 6 + its upgrade-path-only scope.

subtasks.title: Comparable (semver) version of the running binary
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: cmd/stagecoach/main.go has `var version = "dev"` (ldflags-injected) and resolveVersion() which produces a DISPLAY string like "dev (19f4df7-dirty)" — NOT comparable. FR-U5 step 1 + FR-U6 require comparing the running binary's version to the latest release tag (semver). No semver lib is in go.mod today (stdlib only for this is fine — Go's `golang.org/x/mod/semver` is NOT stdlib; implement a minimal compare on `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with optional -prerelease, sufficient for goreleaser tags, OR add golang.org/x/mod as a dep — DECISION: implement a small stdlib-only compare to avoid a new dep, matching the repo's minimal-deps posture).
2. INPUT: main.go's `var version` (the ldflags value) and debug.ReadBuildInfo() (for the VCS fallback). The release tag shape is `vX.Y.Z` (goreleaser .Tag).
3. LOGIC: New package internal/upgrade/version.go (or internal/version) exposing: (a) `CurrentSemver() (tag string, ok bool)` — returns the real semver of the running binary if `version` parses as a release ("0.1.0" or "v0.1.0"); returns ok=false for "dev"/unparseable. (b) `Compare(a, b string) int` — semver compare on vX.Y.Z (handle missing leading v; -prerelease per semver spec). (c) `ParseAndClean(raw string) (normalized string, ok bool)`. Keep main.go's resolveVersion() for display UNCHANGED (it feeds --version); expose the ldflags value to the upgrade package via a setter the upgrade command reads (e.g. upgrade.SetCurrentVersion(version) at startup, or read debug.ReadBuildInfo main version). DECIDE the seam and document it. For a dev build (ok=false), --check reports current display + latest and does NOT claim an update is available (exit 0, informational) — see P1.M4.T2.S1.
4. OUTPUT: New version-compare package + tests (Compare table: 1.0.0<1.0.1, 1.0.0==v1.0.0, 1.0.0>1.0.0-rc1, 2.0.0>1.9.9; CurrentSemver ok=true for release, ok=false for "dev"). go test passes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] package doc comment explaining display-version vs comparable-version distinction.

tasks.title: [upgrade] config table (global-only) + LoadUpgradeConfig seam
tasks.description: Add the optional, additive [upgrade] config table (channel, source_repo) read by the upgrade command from the GLOBAL config file only — without invoking full config.Load (which needs a repo dir and triggers the FR-B3 bootstrap write). Per FR-B4 this additive table does NOT bump CurrentConfigVersion and does NOT emit an upgrade advisory.

subtasks.title: UpgradeConfig struct + global-file-only LoadUpgradeConfig + defaults + global-only ignore
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: internal/config/config.go Config struct + Defaults() (CurrentConfigVersion=3). load.go resolves via 7 layers needing a repo dir; file.go decodes fileConfig. The upgrade command has a NO-OP PersistentPreRunE (it runs outside a git repo and must not trigger config.Load's first-run bootstrap write — v3_scope_boundary.md). So [upgrade] needs a DEDICATED reader, not the full resolver. FR-U10: [upgrade] is global-only; a per-repo .stagecoach.toml [upgrade] is ignored with a --verbose note. FR-B4: additive → do NOT bump CurrentConfigVersion, do NOT emit an advisory.
2. INPUT: internal/config/{config.go,file.go,defaults.go,load.go} and the XDG global config path resolver already used by the file loader.
3. LOGIC: (a) Add `UpgradeConfig` struct { Channel string; SourceRepo string } to config.go (toml:"upgrade" nested under a new [upgrade] table — decode via fileConfig.Upgrade). Seed Defaults(): Channel="stable", SourceRepo="dabstractor/stagecoach" (PRD §16.1 defaults). (b) Add a NEW exported helper `config.LoadUpgradeConfig() (UpgradeConfig, error)` that reads ONLY the global config file (XDG path, the same path resolution as the global file loader) and decodes its [upgrade] table with Defaults applied; it does NOT read repo file/git-config/env/flags and does NOT write/ bootstrap. This is the seam the upgrade command (P1.M4.T1) calls. (c) Document that a per-repo .stagecoach.toml [upgrade] is intentionally NOT read here (global-only). (d) Verify CurrentConfigVersion stays 3 and no load-time advisory fires for a file lacking [upgrade] (add a test: load a global file without [upgrade] → defaults; load one with [upgrade] → merged; an older-version file with [upgrade] still works, no advisory).
4. OUTPUT: Modified config.go/defaults.go/file.go + new LoadUpgradeConfig + tests. go test ./internal/config/ passes; CurrentConfigVersion unchanged.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] add the [upgrade] table rows to docs/configuration.md (channel, source_repo, global-only note) and the inline config.go field comments.

tasks.title: GitHub Releases HTTP client (the named §19 exception) + asset/checksum primitives
tasks.description: The HTTP client that fetches release metadata and downloads the selected archive + checksums.txt, SHA256-verifying it. The ONLY stagecoach surface that makes network calls. Injectable base-URL + *http.Client so tests use httptest, not the real API.

subtasks.title: Release-metadata fetch (latest/all-by-tag/pinned) with optional token auth + error mapping
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/017_397abce9deb1/architecture/external_deps.md §1. net/http is stdlib (no new go.mod dep). API: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest → {tag_name, assets:[{name,browser_download_url,size}], prerelease, draft}; /releases (array, for --prerelease); /releases/tags/{tag} (pinned, --version). Auth: STAGECOACH_GITHUB_TOKEN then GITHUB_TOKEN → 'Authorization: Bearer <t>'. MUST set User-Agent (Go default UA sometimes rejected). FR-U11: network/rate-limit errors abort before any write.
2. INPUT: owner/repo (string, from LoadUpgradeConfig().SourceRepo or --source-repo flag), channel (stable/prerelease), optional pinned tag. A *http.Client and base URL (injectable for tests).
3. LOGIC: New package internal/upgrade/releases.go exposing a `Client` struct { HTTP *http.Client; BaseURL string; Repo string; Token string } and methods: LatestStable(ctx) (Release, error); LatestAdmittingPrereleases(ctx) (Release, error) (filters draft=false, admits prerelease, picks highest semver via P1.M1.T1.S2 Compare); ReleaseByTag(ctx, tag) (Release, error). Release struct: Tag, Assets []Asset{ Name, DownloadURL string; Size int64 }. Errors: typed (ErrNoReleases, ErrRateLimited, ErrHTTP) wrapping status + message; 404→ErrNoReleases; 403/429→ErrRateLimited (hint: set a token). Token resolution: explicit param; the command layer (P1.M4) resolves STAGECOACH_GITHUB_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN env. BaseURL default 'https://api.github.com'; tests inject httptest.Server.URL. Stream-safe (do not buffer whole JSON; or buffer — releases JSON is small).
4. OUTPUT: New releases.go + tests against an httptest fake server (latest returns a canned release; 404→ErrNoReleases; 403→ErrRateLimited; prerelease-filter picks highest non-draft). go test passes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] package doc comment stating this is the SOLE network surface + the §19 scoping.

subtasks.title: Asset + checksums.txt download + SHA256 verification primitives
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: external_deps.md §1-§2. goreleaser checksums file = '{project}_{version}_checksums.txt', one line per artifact: '<64-hex-sha256>  <filename>' (two spaces). Archive names = 'stagecoach_{version}_{os}_{arch}.{tar.gz|zip}'. DownloadURL is browser_download_url (redirects to objects.githubusercontent.com — net/http follows redirects). SHA256 via crypto/sha256 (stdlib).
2. INPUT: A Release (from P1.M1.T3.S1) + target GOOS/GOARCH (runtime.GOOS/GOARCH) + the Client's *http.Client/BaseURL.
3. LOGIC: In internal/upgrade/releases.go (or download.go): (a) SelectAsset(release, goos, goarch) (Asset, error) — map (goos,goarch)→asset-name pattern ('darwin/arm64'→'stagecoach_<v>_darwin_arm64.tar.gz'; 'windows/*'→'.zip'); error if no match (FR-U5 step 3). (b) DownloadFile(ctx, url, dest string) error — stream to dest (multi-MB; do not buffer). (c) FetchChecksums(release) (map[filename]sha256hex, error) — find the '*_checksums.txt' asset, download, parse lines. (d) VerifySHA256(path string, want string) error — compute + compare (constant-time via crypto/subtle). (e) A high-level DownloadAndVerifyArchive(ctx, release, goos, goarch, destDir) (archivePath string, err error) composing select→download→fetch-checksums→verify, returning the verified archive path. On any failure (no asset / checksum line missing / mismatch / network) return a typed error; NOTHING is left except a temp file the caller cleans (FR-U11).
4. OUTPUT: download/verify primitives + tests (httptest serves a canned archive + checksums.txt; verify passes on correct, FAILS on tampered bytes or missing line; SelectAsset picks the right pattern per GOOS/GOARCH). go test passes.
5. MOCKING: httptest server for all download tests; never hit the real API in CI.

milestones.title: Install-method detection + delegation (FR-U2, FR-U3, FR-U4)
milestones.description: Resolve HOW the running binary was installed (the 9-channel detection cascade) and, for non-direct channels, delegate to that channel's own native updater — running it where it is per-user/non-destructive, printing it where it needs privileges (AUR) or is declarative (Nix). Never auto-elevate. Never overwrite a manager-owned binary except via --force.

tasks.title: Install-method detection cascade
tasks.description: detectChannel() — explicit override → package-manager DB query → path heuristics → default direct. Read-only, best-effort, logged at --verbose, bounded by a short timeout so a hung query cannot stall an upgrade.

subtasks.title: detectChannel() cascade (override → PM DB → path heuristics → direct)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: external_deps.md §7. os.Executable() → resolved realpath (filepath.EvalSymlinks) for path heuristics. Channels (FR-U2): brew, scoop, winget, pacman(AUR), npm, mise, asdf, nix, go-install, direct. The npm wrapper sets STAGECOACH_INSTALL_METHOD=npm (external_deps.md §3) — the explicit-override branch reads it. PM DB queries: `brew list stagecoach`, `scoop list stagecoach`/`scoop prefix stagecoach`, `winget list` (Windows), `pacman -Q stagecoach-bin`, `npm ls -g --depth=0`, `mise ls`, `asdf list`. Path roots: Homebrew Cellar (/opt/homebrew/Cellar, /usr/local/Cellar), Scoop shims (scoop\shims), npm global node_modules, Nix /nix/store, $GOPATH/bin (go install), /usr/bin (AUR). Ambiguous → 'direct'.
2. INPUT: os.Executable() + os.Getenv('STAGECOACH_INSTALL_METHOD') + an injected command-runner interface (for tests) + GOOS.
3. LOGIC: New internal/upgrade/detect.go. Define a Channel type (string enum) and `Detect(ctx) (Channel, evidence string, err error)`. Cascade in FR-U2 priority: (a) explicit override env/flag → that channel (validate it's a known channel; flag is passed in by the command layer P1.M4); (b) PM DB queries — each runs via a thin exec wrapper with a context timeout (default ~3s each; skip on GOOS mismatch e.g. winget only on windows, brew/scoop/pacman only where relevant) and parses stdout/exit for ownership; first confirming query wins, return its channel + evidence; (c) path heuristics on realpath(exe) — prefix-match the known roots; (d) default 'direct'. Log each attempted step at --verbose (the command layer passes a verbose flag / logger). NEVER mutate; queries are read-only. Expose an exec-runner seam (interface) so tests inject canned outputs (no real brew/scoop on CI).
4. OUTPUT: detect.go + table/property tests (override wins; each PM-query branch returns its channel on a canned 'installed' stdout and skips on 'not installed'; path-heuristic prefix matches; default direct). go test passes; cross-platform via GOOS guards.
5. MOCKING: injectable exec-runner + injectable os.Executable (pass the exe path in) + injectable GOOS. CI has none of these PMs installed → tests use the injected seams.

tasks.title: Delegation dispatcher (FR-U3 table + FR-U4 run-vs-print)
tasks.description: For a detected non-direct channel, map it to the channel's own updater command and either RUN it (per-user, non-destructive channels) or PRINT it (needs privileges / declarative). Direct channel is NOT handled here — it routes to the direct-swap milestone (P1.M3). Never auto-elevate.

subtasks.title: delegate() — channel→updater table + run-vs-print policy
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: external_deps.md §7 + PRD §9.29 FR-U3 table. Updaters: brew→'brew upgrade stagecoach'; scoop→'scoop update stagecoach'; winget→'winget upgrade stagecoach'; npm→'npm install -g @dabstractor/stagecoach@latest' (detect pnpm/yarn/bun globals and emit matching syntax: if PNPM_HOME/npm config global → pnpm/yarn/bun add -g); mise→'mise upgrade stagecoach'; asdf→'asdf install stagecoach latest' (+ 'asdf global stagecoach latest' if it was global); go-install→'go install github.com/dabstractor/stagecoach/cmd/stagecoach@latest'; AUR→PRINT 'sudo pacman -Syu stagecoach-bin' (or 'yay -Syu stagecoach-bin') — needs root; Nix→PRINT ('nix profile upgrade' / 'nix flake update' on user config) — immutable, no in-place swap. FR-U4: RUN homebrew/scoop/mise/go-install/npm (per-user non-destructive); PRINT AUR(needs root)/Nix(declarative); never auto-sudo. FR-U1: NEVER overwrite a manager-owned binary (delegating means the manager does it).
2. INPUT: A Channel (from P1.M2.T1.S1 Detect) + the upgrade options (yes/verbose) + an exec/streaming runner seam + an output writer.
3. LOGIC: New internal/upgrade/delegate.go: `Delegate(ctx, ch Channel, opts) (DelegateResult, error)` where DelegateResult = { Ran bool; Command string; ExitCode int }. For each run-channel: build the argv, optionally confirm (the command layer P1.M4 owns the y/N prompt; Delegate takes a pre-confirmed bool), exec it streaming stdout/stderr to the writer, return Ran=true + exit code. For print-channels: write the exact command to stdout, return Ran=false + the command string (the command layer exits 0, PRD §15.4 'printed-the-command'). Detect npm variant (pnpm/yarn/bun) by env/config heuristic and emit matching syntax. 'direct' channel is NOT delegated — Delegate returns an error/sentinel (ErrDirectSwap) the command layer routes to P1.M3. If channel==manager-owned AND user passed --force intending a self-swap of a manager binary — that gate is ALSO in the command layer (FR-U1); Delegate itself never self-swaps.
4. OUTPUT: delegate.go + tests (per-channel argv table; run-channel execs via injected runner and returns its exit code; print-channel writes the command + Ran=false; npm-variant detection; ErrDirectSwap for 'direct'). go test passes.
5. MOCKING: injectable exec-runner (returns canned exit codes) + bytes.Buffer output writer.

milestones.title: Direct-binary swap (FR-U5, FR-U7, FR-U8, FR-U11) + --rollback
milestones.description: The ONLY self-swap path, used for the direct (curl|sh / manual-download) channel (or --force). Download the target archive, SHA256-verify against checksums.txt, sanity-run the new binary, back up the prior, atomically rename it into place (Unix) / two-step rename (Windows). Rollback restores the prior backup. Failure at any pre-swap step leaves the on-disk binary byte-for-byte unchanged.

tasks.title: Resolve target + download + verify + extract + sanity-run
tasks.description: The pre-swap half of the direct path: resolve the target release, select+download+verify the platform archive, extract the single binary, and sanity-run it (--version matches target, exit 0) before any swap. Abort on any failure, leaving only a temp file.

subtasks.title: Resolve target release + select GOOS_GOARCH asset
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: FR-U5 steps 2-3. Target resolution: default = latest stable (Client.LatestStable); --prerelease = Client.LatestAdmittingPrereleases; --version <v> = Client.ReleaseByTag(v). Asset selection = SelectAsset(release, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH) from P1.M1.T3.S2.
2. INPUT: Client (P1.M1.T3.S1), channel/version flags, runtime.GOOS/GOARCH.
3. LOGIC: New internal/upgrade/swap.go (or resolve.go): `ResolveTarget(ctx, c *Client, opts) (Release, Asset, error)` composing the right Client method per opts then SelectAsset. Validate the target tag is newer than current via P1.M1.T1.S2 Compare (skip the 'already up to date' case here or in the command layer — DECISION: the --check/up-to-date determination is in the command layer P1.M4.T2; ResolveTarget just returns the chosen release+asset). Error if no matching asset for GOOS/GOARCH.
4. OUTPUT: ResolveTarget + tests (latest/prerelease/version branches against httptest; asset selection per GOOS/GOARCH). go test passes.
5. MOCKING: httptest fake server + injectable Client.

subtasks.title: Download+verify+extract+sanity-run (abort-before-swap on any failure)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: FR-U5 steps 4-6 + FR-U11. Verify = P1.M1.T3.S2 DownloadAndVerifyArchive. Extraction: tar.gz via archive/tar+compress/gzip (stdlib); zip via archive/zip (stdlib) — extract ONLY the single 'stagecoach'/'stagecoach.exe' binary to a temp file, not the whole archive. Sanity-run (FR-U5 step 6): exec '<temp>/stagecoach --version', confirm it prints the target tag and exits 0. A binary that fails to run or misreports is NEVER swapped (FR-U11). Cleanup the temp on the success path is the swap step's job (P1.M3.T2); on failure leave the temp for inspection (PRD) and return an error.
2. INPUT: Release+Asset (P1.M3.T1.S1), Client (P1.M1.T3), a temp dir, an exec runner seam (for sanity-run, injectable in tests).
3. LOGIC: In internal/upgrade/swap.go: `StageNewBinary(ctx, c, release, asset, tempDir) (newBinPath string, err error)` — download+verify to tempDir (DownloadAndVerifyArchive), extract the binary into tempDir/new-stagecoach(.exe), sanity-run it (--version output contains release.Tag, exit 0). Return newBinPath on success; on verify/sanity failure return a typed error and leave tempDir.
4. OUTPUT: StageNewBinary + tests (httptest real archive fixture containing a tiny fake 'stagecoach' script/binary whose --version prints the tag → success; tampered archive → VerifySHA256 fails → error, no extract; a fake binary printing the WRONG tag or exiting non-zero → sanity fails → error). go test passes. Use a compiled stub (cmd/stubcli pattern) as the fake binary so cross-platform tests work.
5. MOCKING: httptest server + a compiled stub binary as the archive payload + injectable exec runner for the sanity-run.

tasks.title: Backup + atomic swap (per-platform) — the on-disk change
tasks.description: The ONLY subtask that changes the on-disk binary: back up the current binary one-deep (.stagecoach-backup / .exe.old) and atomically swap the verified+sanity-run new binary into place. Unix = single os.Rename; Windows = the deferred-delete rename-old/move-new dance. Non-writable target → print the exact sudo command, never auto-elevate.

subtasks.title: Backup + atomic swap (Unix os.Rename / Windows .old dance) + non-writable→print sudo
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: external_deps.md §8 + FR-U5 steps 7-8 + FR-U7. Unix: os.Rename(newTemp, currentExe) is atomic; running process keeps old inode. Windows: running exe is LOCKED — rename current stagecoach.exe→stagecoach.exe.old (Windows allows renaming a running image, not overwriting), move new→stagecoach.exe; clean *.old at next launch. Non-writable (e.g. /usr/local/bin root-owned): detect, leave untouched, PRINT the exact sudo command (FR-U4 — never auto-elevate). Backup is one-deep: '<exe>.stagecoach-backup' (Unix) / the '.exe.old' (Windows); a prior backup is overwritten (FR-U8 — only immediately-prior retained).
2. INPUT: newBinPath (P1.M3.T1.S2) + os.Executable() (the current exe realpath).
3. LOGIC: In internal/upgrade/swap.go: `Swap(ctx, newBinPath string) error`. Steps: resolve current exe (os.Executable + EvalSymlinks); check writability of the target dir/file (attempt a no-op write or check perm); if not writable → return a typed ErrNeedsPrivileges carrying the exact sudo command string (the command layer prints it, exit 0 — PRD §15.4 'printed-the-command'); else: (Unix, build tag _unix) move current → backup path (os.Rename; overwrite existing backup), then os.Rename(newBinPath → current). (Windows, build tag _windows) rename current → stagecoach.exe.old, move new → stagecoach.exe. Also add a startup cleanup (in main or the upgrade command): best-effort delete any stagecoach.exe.old sibling of os.Executable() on Windows (FR-U7). The sanity-run already passed (P1.M3.T1.S2) so the two-file Windows window is clean.
4. OUTPUT: Swap (build-tagged _unix/_windows) + tests: Unix test in a temp dir (swap two real files, assert current now == new content and .stagecoach-backup == old content); non-writable → ErrNeedsPrivileges with the sudo command (chmod the dir unwritable in the test). Windows swap tested via the _windows build on a windows runner (CI matrix has windows-latest) — or unit-test the rename sequence with mockable paths if a real running-exe lock is impractical in-test; at minimum the _windows file compiles and the logic is covered on windows-latest. go test passes on all matrix OSes.
5. MOCKING: temp dirs as the 'exe' for Unix; injectable exe-path resolver.

tasks.title: --rollback (FR-U8)
tasks.description: One-step restore of the immediately-prior backup over the current binary, using the same atomic-swap + sanity-run discipline. No backup → no-op reported as such.

subtasks.title: Rollback: restore prior backup via swap+sanity-run; no-op when none
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: FR-U8. The backup is '<exe>.stagecoach-backup' (Unix) / 'stagecoach.exe.old' (Windows) from P1.M3.T2.S1. Rollback = swap the backup INTO the current exe path, but FIRST sanity-run the backup (a backup whose --version no longer runs is refused with an explanation — FR-U8). Only the immediately-prior version is retained, so rollback is one-step.
2. INPUT: os.Executable() (current exe), the backup path convention.
3. LOGIC: In internal/upgrade/swap.go (or rollback.go): `Rollback(ctx) (restoredVersion string, err error)`. Resolve backup path (exe+'.stagecoach-backup' on Unix; exe+'.old'/stagecoach.exe.old on Windows). If absent → return ErrNoBackup (the command layer prints 'no backup — nothing to roll back' and exits 0, a no-op reported as such, FR-U8). Else sanity-run the backup (--version runs + exits 0); if it fails → return an error explaining the backup is unusable and is NOT swapped. Else Swap the backup into place (reuse P1.M3.T2.S1 Swap, with the backup as the 'new' binary and NO new backup-of-current — DECISION: rolling back does not create a tertiary backup; one-deep is maintained by leaving the now-current as the new rollback target only if we re-back it up — keep it simple: rollback overwrites current with backup, and the previous-current is lost; document this one-step-only semantics matching FR-U8). Return the restored version string.
4. OUTPUT: Rollback + tests (backup present → current becomes backup content; backup absent → ErrNoBackup; backup unrunnable → error + current unchanged). go test passes.
5. MOCKING: temp-dir exe + fake backup binaries (compiled stubs).

milestones.title: CLI surface, run orchestration, and the e2e test harness
milestones.description: Wire everything into the `stagecoach upgrade` cobra command (walled off — no-op PersistentPreRunE, no repo/lock/provider), implement the three run paths (--check, normal detect→delegate-or-direct-swap, --rollback), the confirmation prompt, and the §20.5 e2e self-update scenarios. This milestone makes the feature runnable and regression-safe.

tasks.title: stagecoach upgrade command + local flags + wiring (walled off)
tasks.description: The cobra command, its LOCAL (non-persistent) flags, the no-op PersistentPreRunE that runs outside a git repo and skips config.Load, and registration via init() (zero edits to root.go). Help text disambiguates from the unrelated `config upgrade`.

subtasks.title: cobra upgrade command + local flags + no-op PersistentPreRunE + registration
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See system_context.md §'Conventions'. Register via init()→rootCmd.AddCommand (the lock/hook/integrate pattern) — ZERO edits to root.go. upgrade MUST run outside a git repo and MUST NOT trigger config.Load's first-run bootstrap write (FR-B3) → its PersistentPreRunE is a no-op (mirror internal/cmd/lock.go exactly). Flags are LOCAL to upgrade (Flags(), NOT PersistentFlags) so they do NOT pollute the commit-path flag set. FR-U9 flags: --check/-c, --version <v>, --prerelease, --force, --rollback, --install-method <m>, --yes/-y. FR-U10: --channel <stable|prerelease>, --source-repo <owner/repo> (--prerelease = --channel prerelease). Env: --install-method reads STAGECOACH_INSTALL_METHOD; channel/source-repo read [upgrade] config (global-only via LoadUpgradeConfig). Help/Long MUST disambiguate from `config upgrade` (config-schema migration — two different things).
2. INPUT: internal/cmd/lock.go (the no-op-PersistentPreRunE template), internal/exitcode (UpdateAvailable from P1.M1.T1.S1), config.LoadUpgradeConfig (P1.M1.T2.S1).
3. LOGIC: New internal/cmd/upgrade.go defining `upgradeCmd` (Use:'upgrade', Short, Long disambiguating from config upgrade, PersistentPreRunE: no-op) + local flags bound to package vars (flagCheck, flagTargetVersion, flagPrerelease, flagForce, flagRollback, flagInstallMethod, flagYes, flagChannel, flagSourceRepo). RunE → runUpgrade (P1.M4.T2.S1). init(){ rootCmd.AddCommand(upgradeCmd) }. Validation: --version + --prerelease mutually exclusive; --rollback exclusive with --check/--version; --channel rejects unknown values. Resolve effective channel/source-repo: flag > (env n/a) > LoadUpgradeConfig() > Defaults. Print upgrade-specific help noting it makes network calls to GitHub Releases only.
4. OUTPUT: upgrade.go + a registration test (rootCmd finds 'upgrade'; --help shows flags; running `upgrade` outside a git repo does not error on config and does not bootstrap-write; `upgrade --help` disambiguates from `config upgrade`). go test passes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] add the `stagecoach upgrade` command + its flags + exit codes (0/1/6) to docs/cli.md.

subtasks.title: Confirmation prompt (current→target + action) + --yes skip + run-vs-print output
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: FR-U9. The direct-swap path AND any delegated updater the command RUNS prompt 'y/N' before changing anything (printing current→target version + the action). --yes/-y skips the prompt (scripting). --check and a pure PRINT never prompt.
2. INPUT: current version (P1.M1.T1.S2), target version (resolved release), the planned action string, a TTY/prompt seam + a yes flag.
3. LOGIC: In internal/cmd/upgrade.go (or a prompt helper): `confirmUpgrade(current, target, action string, assumeYes bool, in io.Reader, out io.Writer) (bool, error)`. If assumeYes → true. Else if stdin is not a TTY → default to... PRD: never silently change; DECISION: non-TTY + no --yes → refuse with a message ('re-run with --yes to confirm non-interactively') to match the non-interactive-safety posture. Else print 'stagecoach <current> → <target>\n<action>\nProceed? [y/N]' and read one line; accept only explicit y/Y; everything else (including empty) → false (abort, exit 0 — intentional). The run-vs-print output formatting (delegation PRINT, needs-privileges sudo print) lives here too as shared helpers the orchestrator (P1.M4.T2) calls.
4. OUTPUT: confirmUpgrade + run/print output helpers + tests (assumeYes→true; non-TTY+no-yes→refuse; TTY 'y'→true; TTY 'n'/empty→false). go test passes (inject io.Reader strings; TTY-ness via an injectable isTTY seam).
5. MOCKING: injectable stdin reader + isTTY predicate.

tasks.title: Run orchestration: --check / normal / --rollback paths
tasks.description: The runUpgrade dispatcher that routes the resolved flags+config to the three paths: --check (resolve+compare, exit 6/0), --rollback (P1.M3.T3), and the normal path (Detect→Delegate-or-direct-swap). Resolves GITHUB_TOKEN, the injectable HTTP client/seams, and verbose logging.

subtasks.title: runUpgrade dispatcher (--check / normal detect→delegate|swap / --rollback)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: FR-U1/U4/U5/U6/U12. Build a releases.Client (P1.M1.T3) with Repo=resolved source_repo, Token=resolved (STAGECOACH_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, optional), BaseURL default api.github.com (overridable for tests). --check (FR-U6): resolve target (latest per channel), compare to current (P1.M1.T1.S2); print 'stagecoach <cur> (latest: <latest>; up to date)' exit 0, or 'update available: <cur> → <latest>; run "stagecoach upgrade"' exit 6 (UpdateAvailable). If current is unparseable ('dev'): print current display + latest + 'development build — cannot compare' exit 0 (informational; do NOT claim an update). --rollback: call P1.M3.T3.S1 Rollback; ErrNoBackup→print 'no backup — nothing to roll back' exit 0. Normal path: Detect (P1.M2.T1.S1) → if channel==direct (or --force on a manager-owned binary, with a warning FR-U1) → direct-swap: ResolveTarget→StageNewBinary→confirm→Swap (P1.M3); else Delegate (P1.M2.T2.S1): if Ran → stream its output, exit its code (0 success); if printed → exit 0. Verbose (FR50): log detect steps, resolved channel+evidence, target version, planned action. ALL exit codes from §15.4 upgrade block (0/1/6).
2. INPUT: the upgrade command's resolved flags+config (P1.M4.T1.S1), CurrentSemver (P1.M1.T1.S2), Client (P1.M1.T3), Detect (P1.M2.T1), Delegate (P1.M2.T2), StageNewBinary+Swap (P1.M3), Rollback (P1.M3.T3), confirm+print helpers (P1.M4.T1.S2).
3. LOGIC: New internal/cmd/upgrade.go runUpgrade(cmd, args). Construct Client (Token from env). Branch on flags. For the direct-swap, wire the temp dir (os.MkdirTemp), pass to StageNewBinary, confirm, Swap, cleanup temp on success. Errors → exitcode.New(appropriate) (general→Error/1; --check-behind→UpdateAvailable/6; needs-privileges→Success/0 with printed sudo command). Expose seams (Client/BaseURL, exec-runner, exe-path, isTTY) as package vars defaulting to production impls, overridable in tests — so P1.M4.T3 can drive everything against an httptest server with no real network and no real binary swap.
4. OUTPUT: runUpgrade + wiring + the injectable seams. go build passes; a smoke registration test runs `upgrade --help`.
5. MOCKING: package-var seams for Client/BaseURL, exec-runner, os.Executable, isTTY, stdin — all overridable by P1.M4.T3.

tasks.title: Integration tests + the §20.5 e2e self-update harness
tasks.description: The regression net for behaviors that only manifest against a real (httptest) release source and a real on-disk swap: --check exit 6/0, the direct-swap happy path, failure-safety (bad SHA256 / bad sanity-run abort before swap, on-disk unchanged), --rollback, and delegation refusing a manager-owned binary unless --force. subtasks.title: --check: exit 6 when behind, exit 0 when up-to-date (httptest fake releases)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: §20.5 self-update scenarios + FR-U6. An httptest server serves a fake /repos/{o}/{r}/releases/latest with a canned tag + assets + checksums. Drive runUpgrade with --check via the package-var seams (BaseURL=httptest URL, CurrentSemver injected to an older/newer tag).
2. INPUT: runUpgrade (P1.M4.T2.S1) + the injectable seams.
3. LOGIC: New internal/cmd/upgrade_test.go: (a) current '0.1.0', latest tag '0.2.0' → output 'update available: 0.1.0 → 0.2.0' AND the returned error maps to exit 6 (assert exitcode.For(err)==UpdateAvailable). (b) current '0.2.0', latest '0.2.0' → 'up to date', exit 0. (c) current 'dev' (unparseable) → informational, exit 0 (no update claimed). (d) server returns 404 (no releases) → clear error, exit 1. (e) --check makes NO on-disk change (assert os.Executable untouched / no temp left behind). All via the httptest fake — no real network.
4. OUTPUT: upgrade_test.go --check suite. go test passes; no network.
5. MOCKING: httptest fake releases server; injected CurrentSemver; injected exe path.

subtasks.title: Direct-swap happy path in a temp dir (download→verify→sanity→backup→rename)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: §20.5 self-update scenarios + FR-U5/U7. The fake releases server serves a REAL archive (tar.gz on unix, zip on windows) containing a compiled stub 'stagecoach' whose --version prints the target tag, PLUS a valid checksums.txt. The 'installed binary' is a temp-dir stub whose --version prints the older tag. Inject os.Executable→the temp-dir stub path.
2. INPUT: runUpgrade + seams (P1.M4.T2.S1); a compiled stub binary (cmd/stubcli or a new cmd/stubversion) as both the 'current' and 'new' payload.
3. LOGIC: In upgrade_test.go: set up the temp-dir 'installed' stub at v0.1.0; httptest serves the v0.2.0 archive+checksums (archive built in TestMain or a helper using archive/tar|zip around the stub). Run `upgrade` (normal path, --yes, channel direct via injected Detect→direct). Assert: os.Executable() now resolves to the new binary (its --version == 0.2.0); a '.stagecoach-backup' exists and its --version == 0.1.0; temp cleaned. Cross-platform: tar.gz path on linux/darwin, zip path on windows-latest.
4. OUTPUT: upgrade_test.go direct-swap happy-path test. go test passes on the matrix OSes.
5. MOCKING: httptest server + compiled stub binaries + injected os.Executable/temp dirs.

subtasks.title: Failure-safety + delegation-refuses-manager-owned + rollback (FR-U1/U8/U11)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: §20.5 self-update scenarios + FR-U1/U8/U11. FR-U11: bad SHA256 OR bad sanity-run aborts BEFORE the backup/swap, on-disk binary byte-for-byte unchanged, only a temp file left. FR-U1: a detected manager-owned channel (inject Detect→brew) is NOT self-swapped — Delegate is called; --force is required to self-swap a manager-owned binary (with a warning). FR-U8: --rollback restores the prior backup; no backup → no-op exit 0.
2. INPUT: runUpgrade + seams + the happy-path harness from P1.M4.T3.S2.
3. LOGIC: In upgrade_test.go: (a) tampered archive (wrong SHA256 vs checksums) → runUpgrade errors, on-disk stub unchanged, no '.stagecoach-backup' created, exit 1. (b) archive with a stub whose --version prints the WRONG tag (or exits non-zero) → sanity-run fails → same: unchanged, no backup, exit 1. (c) injected Detect→'brew' (manager-owned), no --force → Delegate is invoked (injected exec-runner records 'brew upgrade stagecoach'), NO swap, the on-disk stub untouched. (d) --force with Detect→'brew' → warning printed AND the direct swap proceeds (swap happens). (e) --rollback with a backup present → current becomes backup content; --rollback with no backup → 'no backup' exit 0. Assert exitcode.For for each.
4. OUTPUT: upgrade_test.go failure/delegation/rollback suite. go test passes.
5. MOCKING: httptest tampered/wrong-version archives; injected Detect + exec-runner; injected exe/temp.

milestones.title: npm wrapper (@dabstractor/stagecoach)
milestones.description: A thin JS package whose postinstall downloads the matching prebuilt native binary from GitHub Releases into a cache (SHA256-verified) and whose bin execs the cached binary — the esbuild/turbo/prisma pattern. The shim sets STAGECOACH_INSTALL_METHOD=npm so `stagecoach upgrade` delegates to npm instead of self-swapping the cached binary.

tasks.description: Author the JS package: package.json (bin, postinstall), the exec shim (sets STAGECOACH_INSTALL_METHOD=npm, spawns the cached binary, forwards argv/stdio/exit), and the postinstall download+verify+extract logic with an --ignore-scripts fallback message.

subtasks.title: package.json + bin/stagecoach.js shim (STAGECOACH_INSTALL_METHOD=npm, exec cached binary)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: external_deps.md §3. The wrapper lives in a new npm/ subdir (keep it out of the Go module root to avoid clutter; or repo root package.json — DECISION: new npm/ subdir containing package.json + bin/ + install.cjs, published via `npm publish npm/`). The cached native binary lives under a versioned cache dir (e.g. npm/<pkg>/node_modules/.cache or os.homedir()/.stagecoach/versions/<v>). Asset names MUST match goreleaser output (external_deps.md §1).
2. INPUT: goreleaser asset-name convention (stagecoach_<v>_<os>_<arch>.{tar.gz|zip}); the version to fetch (resolved from the wrapper's own package.json version, which is bumped per release to match the Go tag).
3. LOGIC: New npm/package.json: name '@dabstractor/stagecoach', version (synced to the Go release tag), bin { 'stagecoach': './bin/stagecoach.js' }, scripts.postinstall 'node install.cjs', engines.node '>=18' (fetch is stdlib https/fs). New npm/bin/stagecoach.js (Node, no deps): (a) set process.env.STAGECOACH_INSTALL_METHOD='npm'; (b) resolve the cached binary path for this wrapper version (and the platform); (c) if absent, print the --ignore-scripts fallback message ('stagecoach native binary not installed (npm --ignore-scripts or postinstall blocked). Install directly: https://github.com/dabstractor/stagecoach#install') and exit 1; (d) else child_process.spawnFileSync(cachedBin, process.argv.slice(2), { stdio:'inherit', env:process.env }) and exit its code.
4. OUTPUT: npm/package.json + npm/bin/stagecoach.js. A local smoke test: place a fake 'stagecoach' binary in the cache path, run `node bin/stagecoach.js --version`, assert it execs the fake and the env tag is set.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] npm/package.json 'description' + a npm/README.md (one paragraph: what the wrapper is, the --ignore-scripts fallback).

subtasks.title: install.cjs postinstall (platform→asset, download+SHA256-verify, extract to cache)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: external_deps.md §1-§3. Platform map: process.platform→goreleaser os (darwin/linux/win32→windows; aix/sunos→unsupported), process.arch→goreleaser arch (arm64→arm64, x64→amd64). Archive: tar.gz (unix) via a tiny JS tar lib OR shelling out to system tar (DECISION: prefer a small JS dep e.g. 'tar' for cross-platform including Windows where tar may be absent — but Node 18+ ships nothing; use the 'tar' npm dep, the wrapper's ONLY dep); zip (windows) via 'yauzl' or Node's experimental zip — DECISION: use the 'tar' package which handles tar.gz and add 'extract-zip' for Windows, OR extract via PowerShell/Expand-Archive fallback. Keep deps minimal and listed. Checksums file = the goreleaser checksums.txt asset; verify the downloaded archive's SHA256 matches the line for the selected asset name.
2. INPUT: package.json version (target release), process.platform/process.arch, GitHub Releases URLs (api + download), optional STAGECOACH_GITHUB_TOKEN.
3. LOGIC: New npm/install.cjs: (a) map platform/arch→asset name + checksums filename for this version; (b) GET the checksums.txt (https.get the browser_download_url, follow redirects), parse the line for the asset; (c) download the asset to a temp file, compute SHA256 (crypto.createHash), compare constant-time; on mismatch → throw (postinstall fails loudly); (d) extract the single stagecoach/stagecoach.exe to the cache dir (mkdir -p); (e) on any error, print a clear message + the direct-install fallback URL and exit non-zero (so the install is visibly broken, not silently half-installed). Honor --ignore-scripts: when postinstall did not run, the shim (P2.M1.T1.S1) handles the missing-binary message.
4. OUTPUT: npm/install.cjs + npm/package.json deps (tar/extract-zip). Local test: point install.cjs at a local file:// or a tiny local http server serving a fixture archive+checksums, assert it downloads+verifies+extracts a fake binary into the cache.
5. MOCKING: local fixture server + fixture archive in npm/test/ (not published).

subtasks.title: CI publish step (npm publish on tag) + version-sync + smoke test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: goreleaser has no npm pipe (PRD §21.2 'Beyond goreleaser'). The wrapper is published by a SEPARATE CI step on tag. The wrapper's package.json version must equal the Go release tag (goreleaser .Version, tag without leading v). An NPM_TOKEN secret (npm automation token) is required for `npm publish`.
2. INPUT: the release tag (from the triggering v* tag), npm/package.json, NPM_TOKEN secret.
3. LOGIC: Add a job to .github/workflows/release.yml (after goreleaser, needs the GitHub Release published so install.cjs can fetch the real binary — though install runs at USER install time, not publish time; publish only ships the JS) that: sets up Node 20, runs `npm version` to sync package.json to the tag (or the version is committed at tag time — DECISION: a tiny pre-publish step reads the tag and writes package.json version, OR goreleaser's before/after hooks do it — keep it as a CI step that sed's the version from $GITHUB_REF), `npm install` (to pin the deps), `npm publish npm/ --access public` with NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=NPM_TOKEN. Add a CI smoke (in ci.yml, not release): `node npm/bin/stagecoach.js --version` against a fake-cached binary to catch shim regressions pre-release.
4. OUTPUT: release.yml npm-publish job + ci.yml shim-smoke step. Document the NPM_TOKEN secret requirement in release.yml comments.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] release.yml + ci.yml inline comments; npm/README.md publish notes.
